avoid_supplements.name: Anticholinergic herbs (Belladonna, Datura, Jimsonweed)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Direct antagonism of cholinergic effects; negates therapeutic benefit and increases risk of myasthenic crisis
avoid_supplements.action: Absolutely avoid; educate patient on anticholinergic-containing supplements

avoid_supplements.name: High-dose Vitamin E (>400 IU/day)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: May potentiate anticoagulant effects and increase cholinergic side effects including GI bleeding risk
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid high-dose supplementation; monitor for bleeding if concurrent use necessary

caution_supplements.name: Magnesium supplements
caution_supplements.mechanism: May enhance neuromuscular blocking effects; theoretical risk of weakness exacerbation in myasthenia gravis
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for increased muscle weakness; separate dosing by 2+ hours if possible

caution_supplements.name: Ginger
caution_supplements.mechanism: May have mild antiplatelet effects; additive with pyridostigmine's cholinergic GI effects
caution_supplements.action: Use cautiously; monitor for increased nausea or GI symptoms

avoid_foods.name: Foods high in anticholinergic alkaloids (nightshade family: peppers, eggplant in excess)
avoid_foods.mechanism: Contain tropane alkaloids that antagonize cholinergic effects and reduce drug efficacy
avoid_foods.action: Limit excessive nightshade consumption; maintain consistent dietary intake

caution_foods.name: High-sodium foods and salt supplements
caution_foods.mechanism: May exacerbate fluid retention and cholinergic-mediated GI effects; increases cramping risk
caution_foods.action: Moderate sodium intake; maintain consistent dietary sodium levels

caution_foods.name: Caffeine-rich foods and beverages
caution_foods.mechanism: Stimulant effects may potentiate cholinergic symptoms (tremor, anxiety, GI motility)
caution_foods.action: Limit caffeine intake; monitor for increased side effects

monitoring_notes: Pyridostigmine has minimal hepatic metabolism and narrow therapeutic window; monitor for cholinergic crisis (excessive salivation, muscle fasciculations, respiratory distress) and myasthenic crisis (weakness). Educate patients to maintain consistent supplement and food intake, avoid anticholinergic agents, and report any changes in symptom control or muscle weakness.
